- agents.md:292-312, 2349-2355, 2607-2613 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: New architectural and log-prefix content was added directly to `agents.md` instead of through an `agents.d/` fragment.
  WHY: This violates CLAUDE.md §30 and risks merge-train conflicts; reviewers disagreed on severity, with MAJOR the highest severity reported.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18526-18567 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The standalone stall-recovery path passes an incomplete PR JSON object, so the helper may not recognize implementation PRs and may dispatch the resolver instead of the re-issue path.
  WHY: The reviewer says the object's missing body and state fields cause the implementation-PR and state checks to fail; severity was not stated.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10379-10382, 18566-18567 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The standalone caller passes a reduced PR object, causing an extra `pulls/<n>` API request per conflicted PR per stall tick despite the full payload being available in `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED`.
  WHY: This contradicts the changelog claim of zero new API calls on the stall path and the §14 audit-before-adding rule.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10384-10388 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Bare `jq` command substitutions can abort the poller under `set -euo pipefail` if parsing fails.
  WHY: A malformed or truncated PR JSON payload can terminate the poller tick before the helper returns; reviewers suggested appending `|| true` or `2>/dev/null || echo ""` to the assignments.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:check-run `static-checks` | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `static-checks` run was cancelled while the ShellCheck loop was running, leaving the aggregate `lint` check red without a real ShellCheck result.
  WHY: The runner shutdown is a cancellation rather than a diagnostic from the diff; a re-run is needed to obtain a result.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15893, 19584 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The managed `close_and_reissue` cases can be reached for a standalone issue and label the replacement `ai:orchestrator-managed` without a tracking issue or wave mapping.
  WHY: The replacement may no longer be watched by standalone stall recovery; the reviewer could not confirm the route end to end.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1409-1437 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `autofix_failure` outer `elif` now matches when `HEAD_BRANCH` is empty, allowing `TARGET_BRANCH` to be set to stable or main where the previous behavior left it empty.
  WHY: The broader behavior may route fixes with a missing `HEAD_BRANCH` for unrelated reasons to stable/main instead of preserving the previous conservative behavior.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:`test_stall_retired_conflict_reissue_is_wired_and_registered` | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The wiring test reads `agents.md` directly to verify log-prefix registry entries rather than reading the assembled-fragment view.
  WHY: Moving the additions into an `agents.d/` fragment would silently break the test, which reinforces the direct-edit violation.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (check-run `static-checks`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The ShellCheck loop over `scripts/*.sh` ended with `##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal`, so the `static-checks` check did not complete.
  WHY: This is a runner cancellation, not a diagnostic from the diff; a re-run is needed to get a real result.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` lines 18566-18567, `_stall_retired_host_only_conflict_check` `"${issue_num}" "${STALL_CONFLICT_PR_NUM}" "${_std_conflict_linked}"`; refetch condition at lines 10379-10382 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The standalone caller passes the reduced object, so the helper always issues one extra `pulls/<n>` read even though `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` already holds the full REST payload on the retry path.
  WHY: Each standalone stall tick on a conflicted PR makes one extra REST call, contradicting the changelog row "New GitHub API calls on the stall path: 0" and the §14 audit-before-adding rule; the suggested fix is to pass `"${_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED:-${_std_conflict_linked}}"`.
- `agents.md` new `STALL_RETIRED_CONFLICT_REISSUE` registry lines and new paragraph under item 8 of "Workflow architecture" | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: New content was added directly to `agents.md`; only the item 14 rewording is a correction to existing text.
  WHY: Direct additions increase merge-train conflict risk, and moving them to a fragment would also require changing the wiring test.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `resolve_merge_conflict` case (line 15893) and managed open-PR guard (line 19584) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The stall judge can reach managed `close_and_reissue` cases for a standalone issue because `local_id` is empty, adding `ai:orchestrator-managed` without a tracking issue or wave mapping.
  WHY: The replacement issue is then no longer watched by standalone stall recovery; the reviewer could not confirm the route end to end.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Fix both standalone and managed stall-recovery paths: when a conflicted host-only path is in the trusted retired-file manifest and absent from the current base, use close_and_reissue to recreate the affected PR against the current base."
  Expected change site: the other places that act on a conflicted PR stuck in `ai:review-blocked`. Candidates are the `dispatch_rb_judge` cases (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15916` and `:19135`) and the managed review-blocked pre-judge conflict dispatch (`_dispatch_review_for_conflicts "${RB_PR}" "${RB_HEAD_REF_PRECHECK}"`, line 23097).
  Evidence of absence: `_stall_retired_host_only_conflict_check` is called at only three sites: lines 15893, 18567 and 19584. A resolver run that fails closed with `sandbox_path_host_only` ends with linked issues labeled `ai:review-blocked`. The cross-pollination report cites the failure-comment script for this (`review_autofix_step_failure_comment.sh:25` and `:36`) and the ladder (`orchestrate_lib.py:1639-1643`) for the stall ladder. I did not open either. The stuck-on-retired-conflict case can still end in repeated judge or resolver dispatch (lines 23097, 22765, 22848) rather than `close_and_reissue`. The explicit "both standalone and managed" wording is met for the three paths touched. This gap concerns only the review-blocked and sweep dispatch sites.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `_stall_retired_host_only_conflict_check`, the `pr_state`/`head_repo`/`head_ref`/`head_sha`/`base_ref` assignments (lines 10384-10388)
  PROBLEM: Bare command substitutions from `jq` could abort the poller on a non-object payload.
  WHY: The helper runs under the poller's shell options; the suggested minimal fix is to append `|| true` to each assignment.

=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- CI status: static-checks failed due to runner cancellation; review findings are contingent on clean CI results.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` lines 18526 and 18567 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The standalone stall recovery path passes an incomplete PR JSON object containing head_ref/sha/repo and base.ref, but lacking the body and state fields.
  WHY: The helper's implementation-PR and state checks fail on the reduced object, so it may treat standalone implementation PRs as non-implementation PRs and dispatch the resolver path instead of the re-issue path.
- `agents.md` lines 292-312 (the Workflow architecture addition) and lines 2349-2355 (log-prefix registry) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: New architectural facts and log-prefix registry entries were added directly to `agents.md`.
  WHY: This violates CLAUDE.md section 30, which mandates use of `agents.d/*.md` fragments to prevent merge conflicts in this high-contention file.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` lines 18526-18567 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The standalone stall recovery path performs an extra per-issue API call to refetch the full PR JSON when the cached version is incomplete.
  WHY: Every standalone stall tick on a conflicted PR makes one extra `pulls/<n>` request, violating the changelog claim of zero extra calls and the §14 audit-before-adding rule.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Fix both standalone and managed stall-recovery paths: when a conflicted host-only path is in the trusted retired-file manifest and absent from the current base, use close_and_reissue to recreate the affected PR against the current base.
  Expected change site: All three dispatch sites for the conflict resolver (managed resolve_merge_conflict, standalone retrigger_review guard, and managed pre-judge conflict dispatch).
  Evidence of absence: The new _stall_retired_host_only_conflict_check is called only at three sites (resolve_merge_conflict, standalone retrigger_review guard, managed early-phase open-PR guard); the review-blocked judge for integration-sync PRs (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:23094-23119) does not consult it, meaning it still dispatches the resolver and fails closed for retired host-only conflicts.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, lines 10384-10388
  PROBLEM: Bare command substitutions for `pr_state`, `head_repo`, `head_ref`, `head_sha` and `base_ref` under `set -euo pipefail` may abort the poller if the payload is non-object JSON.
  WHY: The suggested minimal fix is to append `|| true` to each assignment.
